WITH RECURSIVE ancestry AS (
  SELECT
    c.class_symbol_id,
    c.base_symbol_id,
    1 AS depth
  FROM code.class_bases c
  WHERE c.base_name = 'ApiModel'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    a.class_symbol_id,
    c.base_symbol_id,
    a.depth + 1
  FROM ancestry a
  JOIN code.class_bases c ON a.class_symbol_id = c.class_symbol_id AND c.base_name != 'ApiModel'
),
min_depths AS (
  SELECT class_symbol_id, MIN(depth) AS depth
  FROM ancestry
  GROUP BY class_symbol_id
)
SELECT class_symbol_id, depth
FROM min_depths
WHERE depth >= 2
ORDER BY depth, class_symbol_id;

request:
Which classes inherit from ApiModel (auto_ontology/server/models.py) only indirectly, i.e. through at least one intermediate class of this repository, and do not name ApiModel directly in their class statement? An import alias of ApiModel (auto_ontology/server/responses.py imports it as _Payload) counts as naming ApiModel directly, and a subscripted base such as ListResponse[T] counts as its class. For each, give the class symbol ID and the length of the shortest inheritance chain to ApiModel (2 when the parent class directly subclasses ApiModel).

Requested output columns: class_symbol_id (string), depth (integer).
explanation: The query first finds all direct bases named ApiModel (depth 1). It then recursively follows further bases that are not ApiModel, incrementing depth. Finally it selects the minimum depth for each class and filters to those whose shortest chain is at least 2 (i.e., they do not directly name ApiModel in their class statement, but inherit through at least one intermediate class).

    c.class_symbol_id,

  WHERE c.base_name = 'ApiModel'
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    a.class_symbol_id,
    c.base_symbol_id,
    a.depth + 1
  FROM ancestry a
  JOIN code.class_bases c ON a.class_symbol_id = c.class_symbol_id AND c.base_name != 'ApiModel'
),
min_depths AS (
  SELECT class_symbol_id, MIN(depth) AS depth
  FROM ancestry
  GROUP BY class_symbol_id
)
SELECT class_symbol_id, depth
FROM min_depths
WHERE depth >= 2
ORDER BY depth, class_symbol_id;
